parts.note: craft read as skill, not as a vessel: the art of handling a ship at sea

explanation.surface: Looks like a description of a seagoing ship or boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests a vessel, but here it means skill: the skill of going to sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Seamanship is the skill and expertise of a sailor in managing a ship on the open water.

indicators.note: a shell is the outside, so only the first and last letters are taken

parts.note: outside letters of some
identical means the same

explanation.surface: The husk of some matching seeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shell' looks like a seed's casing, but signals taking the outer letters of 'some'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sesame is a plant whose small oily grains are used in cooking, sprinkled on bread.

indicators.note: destroying a word breaks it apart so its letters can be rebuilt

explanation.surface: Taking revenge for an attack on the Swiss city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retaliate for' takes an object, as 'avenge' does: avenge a wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To avenge something is to inflict harm in return for a wrong suffered.

clue.text: How vowels are used by Artemidorus?

definitions.text: How vowels are used by Artemidorus?

parts.words: How vowels are used by Artemidorus?
parts.note: the name Artemidorus contains each of the five vowels once, in their standard order

explanation.surface: Seems to ask about pronunciation by an ancient Greek writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Spell the name out: A, E, I, O, U appear in sequence, as in the ABC.
explanation.definitionFit: The vowels in that name run in the same order as their place in the ABC.

parts.note: to reach is to stretch out

explanation.surface: A patient arriving at hospital carried on a litter.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the recipe and the description: patients are brought into ER lying on one.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretcher is a portable frame for carrying an injured person, often into casualty.

clue.text: One fanatic seizing power makes contribution

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold of, so the outer letters wrap around power

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast or fanatic
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A zealot grabbing control as their part in some enterprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Input is something put in, a share of ideas or effort given to a project.

clue.text: Too much duck for German fellow

parts.note: OTT is short for over the top, excessive
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, so O

explanation.surface: Complaining that a German man was served too much duck.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT (over the top) is informal British shorthand for excessive; a duck is a zero score in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a common German male first name, so a typical German man.

indicators.note: in puts the letter inside the van

parts.note: the Ford Transit is a common van
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A request to give someone called Mike a lift in a van.
explanation.walkthrough: The Transit is Ford's best-selling van in Britain; Mike is radio code for M.
explanation.definitionFit: To transmit is to pass on or convey, as a signal or a disease is carried.

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece beneath another comes after it

parts.note: in Greek myth Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to his beloved Hero

explanation.surface: A romantic hero's sweetheart standing under an ancient tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hero' is the priestess of Greek legend, not a brave man; Leander was her lover.
explanation.definitionFit: The oleander is an evergreen flowering shrub or small tree of the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Mix correct as we use condiment

indicators.note: to mix is to stir together, so these letters are combined anew

explanation.surface: Kitchen instructions to blend the right amount of a sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: Fodder is CORRECT AS WE USE; 'Mix' reads as a cooking direction but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the spicy brown vinegar-based sauce added to food for flavour.

parts.note: the Barbarians rugby side are nicknamed the Baa-Baas; read literally, baa-baas are bleating animals that follow blindly

explanation.surface: Seems to mock the unthinking fans of the Barbarians rugby club.
explanation.walkthrough: The Barbarians are a famous invitational British rugby team, nicknamed the Baa-Baas; read as a nursery word, baa-baa is the bleating animal itself.
explanation.definitionFit: People who follow others unthinkingly are called sheep, and the woolly animals themselves say baa.

clue.text: Depraved sort Royal Engineers will copy?

parts.note: RE is the abbreviation for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
probate is the officially certified copy of a will

explanation.surface: Asks whether a corrupt person will imitate the army engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' reads as a verb, but it is the legal document; probate is the court-proved copy of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprobate is an unprincipled, immoral person, someone of corrupt character.

clue.text: Traveller in storm on Russian plane

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter aircraft
to storm is to rant, shout angrily

explanation.surface: A passenger caught in bad weather aboard a Russian aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storm' looks like weather, but it is a verb meaning to rage, RANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A migrant is someone who moves from place to place, often for work, so a traveller.

clue.text: Sherwood friar with fault eats heartily

parts.note: Friar Tuck is Robin Hood's companion in Sherwood Forest
a sin is a moral fault

explanation.surface: The famously greedy friar's failing is that he eats a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: Friar Tuck, of the Robin Hood legends, is traditionally portly, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To tuck in is an informal idiom for eating food with enthusiasm and appetite.

indicators.note: replaced here means put back in a different arrangement, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Asks in which state a man had his hip replacement operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Replaced' reads as surgery, but it signals rearranging the letters of WHERE MANS HIP.
explanation.definitionFit: New Hampshire is one of the fifty United States, in New England.

clue.text: Charlie in riotous romcom is miniature model

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the scrambled letters
riotous means wild and disorderly, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A character in a hilarious romantic comedy plays a small replica.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' looks like the link to the definition, but it belongs to the rearranged letters; 'riotous' sounds like a review of the film.
explanation.definitionFit: A microcosm is a small world that represents a larger whole in miniature.

clue.text: Mean to consume mostly raw fish

indicators.note: to consume is to swallow, so these letters take the next inside

parts.note: mean means stingy, tight with money

indicators.note: mostly drops the final letter of the word raw

explanation.surface: A tightfisted diner deciding to eat a seafood dish almost uncooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like a verb (to intend), but it is the adjective for being tight with money.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingray is a flat sea creature with a venomous barbed tail.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to expose to danger
second meaning, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as END ANGER and it is the advice a peacemaker gives.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger is to threaten or imperil; split in two, it urges stopping rage.

parts.note: services read as serves in a game on court, not the armed forces

explanation.surface: Seems to ask about military kit used by the armed forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The services' suggests the army, navy and air force; here it means a player's serves.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is the strung bat each player uses to hit the ball, including when serving.

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a setter is a dog breed, and a new one is a pup

explanation.surface: Seems to back a newly arrived crossword compiler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the puzzle compiler; it is the gundog, and a young one is a PUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To prop up is to hold something in place so it does not fall, to bolster it.

clue.text: On the radio, male voice for £10

indicators.note: something heard on the radio is only heard, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a tenor is a high male singing voice

explanation.surface: A male singer broadcasting a tune for a small fee.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenner is the informal word for ten pounds sterling, or a banknote of that value.

clue.text: I rang AA — convertible in river!

indicators.note: convertible means able to be changed into another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A motorist whose convertible broke down in a river calls the AA for help.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is the British motoring breakdown service; 'convertible' looks like the car, but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The Niagara is the North American river that flows over the famous falls.

indicators.note: found in says the letters are concealed within the following words

explanation.surface: A modification spotted in the terms of a contract.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter is to modify or make different, a synonym for to change.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to keep a rule or festival, to abide by it
second meaning: to look at attentively

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like one instruction to a sentry, but each is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: One verb covers both honouring a custom or law and noticing something by looking.

indicators.note: got it wrong suggests a muddle, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A singer who has messed up an operatic part.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram fodder runs across 'role' and 'got it', leaving 'wrong' as the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigoletto is Verdi's opera about a hunchbacked court jester.

clue.text: Penny in loveless marriage finds release

indicators.note: in places the penny inside the remaining letters
love is zero in tennis, so the O is taken away

parts.note: a union is a marriage

explanation.surface: Penny escapes an unhappy marriage without love.
explanation.walkthrough: Love means zero in tennis scoring, the letter O; 'loveless' removes it, leaving UNIN, and P goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To unpin is to set free by removing a fastening, a form of releasing something.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a tale, often a long or tall one
second meaning: spun fibre used in knitting or weaving

explanation.walkthrough: A story with a thread sounds like a plot line; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarn is both a spun strand for knitting and an informal word for a rambling tale.

parts.note: curtains is slang for the end, death, so this is whoever brings death to people

explanation.surface: Sounds like someone delivering new drapes to our home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curtains' looks like soft furnishings, but it is slang for the end of life.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure personifying death, with a scythe, comes to take each person at their end.
